HOTEL_HILBERT.cr:
a film by Marlene Wetzel & Max Soroca
after Jorge Luis Borges, »August 25, 1983«
with Dietrich Kuhlbrodt and Helena Hauff
HOTEL_HILBERT.b:
Room 19. The old man has been waiting a long time for the younger one, who has already been here.

Every room is taken. There is always room for one more guest.

The 25th of August is the last day the world turned without me. If a world goes out when the one who sees it closes his eyes, where does the day go that came before he opened them?
HOTEL_HILBERT.ghost:
Maria Kodama

Sehr geehrte Frau Kodama!

{ow:N|M}ein Name ist Max Soroka. Ich wurde am 26. August 1983 geboren.

Der 25. August 1983 war der *letzte* Tag dieser Welt, an dem ich noch nicht ~~hier war~~ selbst hier weilen durfte. Gab es diesen Tag überhaupt? Oder beginnt und endet die Welt mit dem eigenen Erscheinen und *Verschwinden*?

Ein alter Freund hat ~~sich selbst~~ den Borges gespielt. Er sagte: Nein, ich will den Borges spielen!

Ich habe mich bis heute nicht getraut, um Entschuldigung zu bitten.

Ein Hotel mit unendlich vielen Zimmern, restlos ausgebucht. Doch mit einem Mal erscheint ein weiterer Gast.{p} Was also tun?

Mit freundlichen Grüßen,
*Max* ~~Soroka~~ Saroka

FAG_BUTTS_IN_THE_FIRE_BUCKET.cr:
directed by Max Soroca & Vanessa Ivan
commissioned by Ninja Tune
FAG_BUTTS_IN_THE_FIRE_BUCKET.b:
In June 2018 they filmed a woman on a heath that had turned violet. She has since gone through the frames one by one and cannot say whether the colour was added later or was already in the heather when they arrived.

Two films were cut from the same material. The first was delivered, approved and released under another name. The second she kept in a bucket of the kind that hangs beside the doors of old houses, for the cigarette ends of guests. She mentions the bucket because it is the only object in this account of which she is certain.

Years later she took the second film out and counted its frames. There were one hundred and ninety-two. The following evening there were fewer; on the third, more. She wrote the numbers down. They do not add up, and she has stopped expecting them to.

On Helgoland it is said that when someone drowns, something climbs out of the sea: black, with eyes the size of plates and a coat of sheepskin. It does not walk; it rolls. It lies across stairs and in the corners of barns. When misfortune has come to a house, the islanders say: Det bisterk Ding lag auf dem Weg.

She does not claim the two are connected. She only notes that on the night she first counted the frames, something was lying on her stairs, and that she stepped over it.

BUBBLE_BOY.b:
It began with a few lines typed into a phone on an August evening in 2018. The phone did not know a single word of them and underlined every one in red.

A month later a small crew drove through Athens and Piraeus with a list: streets through the windscreen, through the rear window, from the side; a playground near the central station; a fire in Exarchia, if it could be had. Beside the bubble the notes say only: artificial, afterwards?

The bubble never came, and neither did the boy. What stayed is a young woman in a tiger-striped top on a street, a dance in front of a grey wall that leaves copies of itself in the air, a city seen through smeared glass, a storm standing over the mountains behind the houses.

At the end a street of parked cars folds into itself, turns round like a kaleidoscope and closes. Perhaps that is the bubble after all, the round shape the film draws around her in its last minutes.

INSANE_IN_THE_BRANE.s: on the quest for reality · documentary essay · 2020
INSANE_IN_THE_BRANE.cr:
an idea by Max Soroka
narrated by Alexa Materna
made without a budget, with master's students in media studies at TU Berlin
INSANE_IN_THE_BRANE.b:
A woman called Alexa set out to find out whether the world is real. She began in a cave, because that is where the question begins, and climbed out into the Allgäu, to the village where Konrad Zuse once lived and wondered whether space itself might be calculating.

The son of the man who built the first computer told her that it might. A professor of artificial intelligence thought the universe too large to be simulated. A theorist of glitches, a pataphysician who has no brother, a parapsychologist and a sheikh each answered a different question.

Somewhere in the film a person stares at a blue summer sky until they find a pixel in it. Nobody has explained that pixel.

The copy kept here measures 176 by 144 pixels and runs for sixty-eight minutes and forty-six seconds.
INSANE_IN_THE_BRANE.pixel: Well, I do spot a pixel there.
book: Where...am I? What's that all? Am I in a cave? Or am I just a shadow in a cave? And what am I? Am I even real? And if so, what is reality basically?

Hi. I'm Alexa. I'm currently on the quest for reality. Do you like to join me? I am often wondering what everything is about and what it means to be here. About what is holding the world together. In its inside but also in its outside.

And the role of us human beings in that. Just a minute ago, I was in a dark, sort of scary place. Comparable to Plato's Allegory of the Cave. There he describes that we may just sit inside a cave without being able to perceive reality but only shadows of things passing by. Not much uplifting, such an idea. I better get back to light.

To nature. To the mountains. Here in Allgäu - In Hinterstein to be precise, was living Konrad Zuse, the inventor of the computer, for some years after World War II. He is also considered as one of the forerunners of Digital Physics. This postulates that the cosmos is finite and therefore countable. In his paper Calculating Space Zuse even claims the universe itself might be a gigantic computer.

Now I'm a bit confused. But let us ask his son Horst Zuse straightforwardly. Well, Calculating Space, it implies the idea: How is the universe structured? The bits as the basic principle and smallest unit of information. This has been maintained until today. The bit lengths and the number of registers and memory sizes have changed but in general - and this is the astonishing thing about - computer are still working according to his principle.

This idea haunted him. So if this is the basic unit of my machine, how is the universe structured then? There are also particles. There are also particles which are able to take two different stages: 0 and 1. And then it is the question of how do these particles correspond with each other? Can it be defined as 0 and 1 as well? If the universe consists of binary units which truly communicate with each other, I better ask that question in a different way: Isn't the universe a gigantic computer by itself if it really functions in that way?

Thus he hypothesized the universe communicates with itself, that particles communicate with each other and hence creative processes can occur through this. So isn't the universe a gigantic computer then? Consisting of billions upon billions of very, very tiny processors? That can communicate with each other? The great success actually happened in 2006 when Deutsche Technikmuseum did a symposium on Calculating Space in honor to Konrad Zuse. That was when Seth Lloyd from MIT showed up saying in the end: "Well, I didn't know so far that Konrad Zuse made a publication already in 1967 and 1969, which contained the topic we are dealing with now - the digital universe.

But, ladies and gentlemen, that key question for all of you would be: Is he right or is he not right? Is the universe a gigantic computer?" Suddenly It went dead silent and the answer was: Yes. He is right. It's not just a gigantic PC. It is a gigantic quantum computer.

Every simulation is a simplification of reality. So the question is how much can I simplify that the answer of the computer is still useful or beneficial? Is it possible that the universe is a simulation? Like in Matrix? I don't think so because according to current discoveries of physics scales we are arguing with are very big up, which means the universe is incredibly huge but also scales downwards are incredibly vast. The smallest unit of time which can be represented is 10 to the power of -42.

It can't be any smaller. We call it Uncertainty of Time, discovered by Max Planck. So this is the reason why there are so many orders of magnitude between the smallest and the largest in the universe that no computer today could even come close simulating an entire reality. Right, so lets take it serious. We we would need a gigantic computer. Every tiny compartement of the universe should be represented inside of this computer.

Everywhere we look at must be something to detect. That computer must be way bigger than the universe. You will need an infinite number of electrons in storage units for simulating a single electron. This means that we can't be a simulation in our universe. But of course we can wonder if an incredible larger universe is existing somewhere containing a gigantic supercomputer, as gigantic and as fast we won't ever be able to build in our "small" universe. Whew.

Lets take it slow. Therefore, the universe is a computer. But what was that simulation thing about? Do we exist inside of a world simulated by a future civilization? Like in a computer game? Raúl Rojas doesn't seem to believe in this.

But other and also prominent people in science and technology rather do. For example Nick Bostrom, a Swedish bestselling writer and professor of philosophy at Oxford University. His so-called Simulation Hypothesis virtually transfers Plato's Allegory of the Cave into a more modern and techy version, so to speak. Lets rather ask a futurologist and writer of science-fiction novels to explain this idea. Well, he's tying this in with his thoughts on superintelligence: Saying that some kind of artificial intelligence will be developed on Earth in future. So we have to be prepared for the fact that there are artificial intelligences in the cosmos which are extremly superior to us.

And that such an intelligence could simulate a whole cosmos. So he argues that either rational beings will never reach a state of development in which they produce real, high-level artificial intelligence or superintelligence. Or maybe, that, for some reason, those cannot exist in the universe or if such intelligences evolve, they can either start simulating - that is, to build other beings of intelligence in extra worlds or not. He considers the latter to be improbable. He suspects that these artificial intelligences - from now on I'll call them Cosmic Superintelligences - so when these Cosmic Superintelligences are able to build up simulated worlds and within these simulated worlds would evolve new simulating superintelligences, so that you would find whole hierarchies of simulated worlds and then on the other hand, it would be obvious that we don't live in the one true world which created the first super intelligence but somwhere far out in the hierachy of derived simulated worlds. Wow.

Nice, very nice. So what is this showing us? It is showing us something about technology, so that we believe we could develop such technology for simulating whole worlds. This is showing us a lot about our times, when we develop the idea of thinking to live in a simulation. So in that respect it is meaningful. In our universe It simply is the case that there is a lower limit, indicated by Quantum physics.

Furthermore, the universe is finite - this is indicated by regular physics which is making it hard to achieve in our universe. But in case you imagine the universe with some extra dimensions - so there would be more space to build such of a computer and the true universe within such a computer could be built is a continuous one instead of a discrete one like in quantum physics, so it could be conceivable for the time being. The idea that one is living in a computer game, in reality, that someone is simulated or whatever you like to call it, could you imagine something like that?

Of course I can imagine something like that, but I wouldn't like to live in a computer world. I can imagine anything. But I live in our world using my five senses and my mind and of course I cannot perceive the dance of the atoms, I intellectually understand how complex life is. But the world I experience with my senses is a true one. and simulated worlds attract me in cinema only. I could do a little test. I'll be very fast doing this.

Trying to check if the computer which is running the simulation is able keep up. Let me try again. Zack. The computer are either very, very powerful. Or it is real after all. This might be all true by itself.

But does it convince us? Personally, it does not seem to be watertight for me. But neither I could disprove it. Or can I? Or is it only theatre? Cinema? Spectacle? After all, this question has been on our minds since primeval times, since we have been able to think and reflect on ourselves.

Creating an image of reality seems to be as ancient as human culture. Whether in prehistoric cave paintings, in Greek tragedies or in dystopian sci-fi-novels and nowerdays in cinema and virtual reality. The idea of simulation may solely be a web of popular culture. So let's ask two clever people who will for sure have a lot to say on that. Appropriately enough, both share almost the same name. So who is simulating whom in here basically?

We can talk about that for very long time - of course on a quite abstract and theoretical level - whether what I can see is real or not meaning: Could it be an illusion somehow? That is an old philosophical debate. For example Déscartes has already considered in a very famous thought experiment if the world could merely be a delusion of a malevolent demon?

Later it became the idea of the Brain in a vat and movies like Matrix, Vanilla Sky, Open Your Eyes and so on. In terms of film history, the idea of cyberpunk was a paradigm shift towards the way science-fiction was discussed in film. Earlier, science-fiction was more clean, very white, very positively progressive, even if aliens were attacking. But with the idea of cyberpunk, some kind of Film noir has come back whichs means that there is a dark world in which a lost and lonely hero is fighting with a crushing superiority which determines daily life. Blade Runner can definitely be taken as the protoype cyberpunk movie. In the early 1990s the element of virtual reality was added and in my opinion everything culminated in Matrix, shot by the Wachowski sisters back then.

(Brothers at that time) Brothers at that time, right. The idea falls back to Fassbinder's World on a wire and the novel on which the movie was based, the idea that someone is living within a simulation. It took visually a lot of what the cyberpunk genre has been laying down over the last 15 years, i.e. a dystopia which is encoded often in a critical way towards capitalism pointing that the all-dominant social structures capturing people within a sort of spectacle without letting them think about it and therefore not letting humans break free what is perhaps the realphilosophische idea behind the whole thing. There is this thought experiment by Robert Nozick in which you are asked to have take opportunity of being connected to a so-called "experience machine". Once connected you will be in a completely simulated world. What is making his version of that thought experiment special is that it will be an absolutely wonderful and fantastic world.

Whatever you need - it will be fulfilled and you will become totally happy. He has asked many people if they like to be connected to that machine. But many people said no. And if you're thinking about the reason why they did so, you will understand that humans are not only concerned about being happy in their lifes. But we are rather keen on living an authentic life. Not like wearing a mask with what we disguise ourselves in daily life, taking on some persona, some fake identity, but contributing ourselves through our authentic self into authentic contexts where other people appear theirselves in a way.

Yet I do think we are living in a simulation which appears like truth for us. I think it's a plausible theory, that will perhaps be verified by the year of 2200. Of course it is possible that everything is simulated. And the higher power or higher force is maybe be the only truth. All the characters of World on the Wire and Simulacron-3 do think they would live in the "true" world. Through a twist in the story and its entanglements, that our main character finds out to be just a character in a simulation.

Means we've layered simulation on simulation and that's probably where we are close to Plato's Allegory of the cave, to what extent you are able perceive what's real. That is to say, even if the upper level would be reached again, that is, the simulation, in which we know that it is even controlled beyond that - so who can tell us that what is intervening from above is actually real, or yet another simulation? So whoever is installing those simulators or whatever, doesn't interest me either. I don't know either how ecstasy is produced. I only know that ecstasy is also taking me to another world. If you are staring at the blue summer sky, staring at very exact, then you can try to check if the colored dots are basically pixels.

Are they pixels? Well, I do spot a pixel there. No idea why. When we think of computer games and argue that these are virtual and simulated worlds as well, we would have to say all glitches and bugs indicate that we are living within a simulation. If our world is to be a simulation, we should be able to observe glitches and bugs here as well. So we also ought to observe errors within our world.

It is maybe a matter of opinion. Well, I guess that almost everybody already experienced something like: Something can't be true seeming like a weird coincidence, there must be something behind - so it would represent something. Or something trivial like when you are walking in the streets while noticing someone you know. But then you realize it wasn't the person you thought of though five minutes later you meet the person nevertheless. A precursor was sent! Something like that could be such a typical glitch in a computer simulation, showing that the software didn't work correctly.

If we could determine this on a physical level, we would have a certain proof that we are inside a simulation. In this case we would have to contact The Institute for Frontier Areas of Psychology and Mental Health at the University of Freiburg where scientists work with anomalistic methods to collect such phenomena. Yes, it is an exciting topic. Ok, so let's call them. People are for example frequently reporting a precognitive encounter. Most of them can be linked to particular situations of crisis.

For example when a person forsees a particular person dying. Or people report inexplicable object movements - even of large objects. Such moments can be quite disturbing so that some people have trouble to integrate this into their existing view of the world. That for we have a consulting service at our institute. For example one appropriate way to explain might be, to say, well, in such moments when a large object seems to move inexplicably - those objects are frequently associated with a particular meaning for this person for a certain period of time, for a moment. Here seems to be kind of entanglement correlation between the person and the environment or co-world.

This can mean psychological tensions that have not been lived out could be released in this way into environment. This can be very similar to psychosomatic illnesses. The question of what's real is posed either in dreams as in simulations. In that sense, Zhuang Zhou's Butterfly Dream was an important discovery for me. It goes like - Zhuang Zhou is dreaming he's a butterfly flying from blossom to blossom. Later he wakes up being Zhuang Zhou.

Asking himself: But maybe I am still this butterfly who thinks to be Zhuang Zhou. This means that we don't even know if we truly are ourselves or if we are just a simulation of ourselves. Or someone else's dream. In the past it was supposed to be the dream of god or of a butterfly. It often was linked with the particular media of these times. During times when the most exciting media for the people was theatre, the simulated world was imagined in a theatrical way, so to speak.

Or gods are watching us and we do a drama performance for them in which they perhaps intervene a bit. I think we're not getting anywhere at this point. Olaf Müller is spotting pixels in the sky but has no idea why. Everybody is talking about these glitches and bugs. There are even whole scientific institutions investigating frontier and parascience phenomena. It seems to be the right moment - the Kairos in the words of Ancient Greeks and Plato, to take matters into our own hands.

Luckily we got Brian helping us. He is, lets say, zombie'pataphysicist and invites us to a cybernetic seance. We gather in the anechoic chamber. Or Dead Room in other words. Can we find a glitch in there? Or can we even get in touch with a simulator? Be careful not stepping on it.

We are neither dead nor alive. We are neither there nor not there. We are in the twilight of death and life. We are beings of the shadow. If He does not exist, thus we do not exist either. We are shadows of God.

You will recognize reality only when once you are dead. Die before you are dead. Only the dead know what reality is. Those who think to be alive in this world have no idea of reality. No matter what kind of professor they are. Anything they have studied at schools is not real either.

Neither knowledge is. Anything that disappears cannot been real. Some spiritual leaders maintain that God would be inside of them. They taste a bit of truth, but they interpret and identify it through a lie. With the help of a lie. Because they are lying if they pretend to be God or argue that God is inside of them.
There is no proof. We are appearances. Appearances of truth. We are shadows of our Lord. Images of the shadow. And we are living a shadow life.

We have been given a shadow life of His real life. And if He likes to take it back, similar to the light - so when the light retreats, anything existing will be lost. And will disappear from the bright spot. We have people reporting us a bright light once in visions of near death. Near-death visions are experiences that occur near death or in people who are in a very weakened state of health but still are conscious. It means that they still can talk about their cognistions in almost realtime.

It can be an experience of light or the sound of a supernatural music. It further can be a view into a supernatural landscape, or perceiving deceased confidants or mystical religious figures who show up apparently to prepare the person for death. Or even for picking up that person. We can find all these elements in so-called near-death experiences with the difference that in this case the person is unconscious, seeming to be inanimate while experiencing these things and able to report about afterwards only when conscious again. But similarity of the experienced elements is already a sign link these phenomena with each other. I even know few reports of people witnessing a near-death experience and while still talking about, witnessing a near-death vision at the same time with same figures.

Those signs show us that such unusual experiences near death should not be seen isolated but in a larger overall context. It wouldn't be right to think near-death experiences are defined accurately what would make it explainable in a certain way. I think we should rather embed near-death experiences in a larger context of different unusual phenomena while keeping the overall picture in mind. So I advise you, fellow philosophers and scientists - Better don't go headfirst through the door. The door won't open that way! You will go mad but the door won't open.

Again and again your head against the door, again and again your head against the door. This kind of door - the door of truth - won't open through head butts. Our existence inside the universe, Big Bang existence, means existence in shadows. Where do you think to find reality in an existence in shadows? Who is the owner of donkey's shadow? Tell me!

For example, we have the theory of a multiverse. It proposes that we are living inside a universe which is just one part of reality, because also other universes exist that were possibly created during Big Bang. So if it is an infinite number of universes, the probability of an exact copy of our universe anywhere is not zero. This says that even a universe could exist, where we are doing an interview right now as well. You need to find the lapse in this train of thought at this point. It goes along with the idea of having an infinite number of monkeys randmoly hitting the keys of a keyboard or of a typewriter and at some point a play of Shakespeare will inevitably show up.

I think the probability of this happening is so low and in the realm of the impossible, making it infeasable basically. Mathematics consists of probabilities. Even mathematics doesn't involve absolute reality. So what do you like to achieve if you are trapped within these probabilities, in this worlds of probabilities? We have to investigate on that from any direction. And that's why we can find so many different formalisms.

Like in physics today we have string theorists and scientists who disagree with that and prefer gravitational physics. Others try to reconcile gravity and quantum mechanics through investigating in Brane Cosmology or Loop Quantum Theory and so on. I think these are different models to understand reality. All of them are valid but reducing the world to one of these theories of information processing is premature because so far we don't know the laws of the universe well enough. Maybe we will never entirely know them. And therefore we will always need to rely on different approaches to analyse reality.

And simulation is one of these approaches. But it can't be everything. Are you thinking as well that we live in a computer? Living a computer life? Then first of all you have to believe that an inventor of this computer exists. Who believes in the computer, has to believe in an inventor of the computer, too.

There is you, oh Lord. So do we live in the brain of God since the computer revolution has started? Or did your father come across the brain of God? Well, the concept of God has almost never showed up with him. It has actually nothing to do with the fact he did not go to church. But the term of god did not exist for him, I would say.

What we have in mind nowerdays when going to church has a totally different role than in science. We won't get further if we say that god exists. It is explainable. Even if we do not know how, but we can explain more and more and there are no limits at the moment that we won't be able to do so. There is no indication that god is sitting somewhere pondering of setting up the laws of nature. No!

One aspect is fascinating me a lot at the moment. It is that we describe the universe in physics as incredibly beautiful representing insanely wonderful symmetries at its deepest level. It constantly thrilled physicists and mathematicians sense of beauty. Then you can simply argue that it must be an awesome algorithm, coded by someone, so the programmer set it up for us. And that programmer has to be Goddes of course. I am Marie-Eve Levasseur.

I am artist. I have always been an artist. Thematically, there is a central theme running through my works. I work at the interface of human and machine. I am working with 3-D animation. I can simulate objects there, physical properties, a world.

There I can choose all the parameters. I am Svenja Anhut. I am game designer and artist. Game designing means to be the person setting up the rules of the game. Without specific rules and fixed mechanics is no game in that sense. They define how the game is flowing, what kind of actions you can do, what kind of you can't do and how you can reach goal.

You are designing the tools the player is free to use to achieve a certain goal, to solve problems, what does it look like, what's the setting? Are you a simulator, then? Well, yes, you are designing a game simulation. But it's controlled by someone from the outside. Namely the gamers. I use Blender, an open source software where every parameter is connected to formulas.

It is very fascinating because you simply can decide everything. How much an object weighs, whether there is gravity or not, whether there is wind or not, if it should be liquid or like rubber. So you can simulate the human body, or other bodies, or plants. This is fascinating. I don't think that we are simulated. Or that the world is a computer.

I don't think so. If it would be a simulation, it would be a damn good one. Anything I feel I feel differently each time. My perception of environment has changed from time to time so if that would be simulated - and I think it's the same for everyone from child to adult or from one location to another - the way we perceive other people, animals or the environment is changing. So first of all, I cannot imagine that it would be possible to simulate perception, feelings, haptics etc., so well that you could want to replace it. The last time I was gaming was around five years ago or so.

For example GTA. There you can drive cars, hit people and shoot them down and stuff. You can earn missions and money. So it basically feels like real life. Almost. If you try to separate computer games and everyday world from each other, you will find out that there are possibilities of rule-making in virtual worlds or in simulations, in computer games, which will differ a lot.

For example, I can cancel out gravity or I can create worlds that consist of two dimensions only, where I can't move upwards, only sidewards - to the front and to the back. Or I can create laboratorial situations of human coexistence, like in "Sim City" or "Civilization" where you can simulate either its own history or the organization of a community or a city which will work according to a certain set of rules then. When I enter a game, I have to follow certain rules by certain specifications. But taking the step into a game or not is the actual free decision. And furthermore, the step out of the game. If we assume that we are trapped in a simulation in the first place, that whether a good or evil god or some dark forces threw us into, the element of freedom is omitted and it is only an apparent freedom.

Well, for me I would consider it very much as a dictatorship. Because a simulation is always designed and developed by its creators and you wouldn't have much opportunity on your own to shape the whole thing, besides making decisions as gamer to reach a certain goal. But always have the prefabricated elements that are given. The fundamental question is imposed by the thesis of whether the Cosmos, the world, has had its beginning in space and time and whether space and time itself has started in Big Bang. And the question on the interior of what the universe is expanding or shrinking automatically brings us to the assumption of an "exterior", within the "interior" could appear as a way of simulation or delusion. It is a fundamental question which cannot be thought without theology or religion, because all religions always suspected that for creation of mankind.

Whether we will merge into nothingness or a better world in which we will enter. Well, maybe we have to give up chasing for evidences at this point. At least for evidences, that might lie beyond our imagination in extra dimensions or on such branes. The idea if I could be somehow simulated could rather affecting me on a less abstract, more tangible level: Culturally. Politically. Socially.

Are you gonna join me for daily routine? I don't think we live in a simulated reality. But reality is very individual. There could be eight billion possibilities out there. Because everyone is sensing it different. Apart from that we have plenty of science-fiction movies that inspired us and we imagine: What if? In "real" world you already feel like being in a simulation often.

Solely because of social limitations that you have, to which you have to subordinate yourself, or how much it is shaping the people around you. I think that the simulated parts are basically our cultures. So we are organized as human beings in different cultures, in certain patterns. You go to work because you have to go, because otherwise you can't afford rent - you have to be functional. And functioning actually follows to be caught inside that pattern. And I think that is somehow the simulated, because if you break out of this pattern like going on a pilgrimage or whatever - you can find a completely different reality.

So I think reality and truth is happening up here. It is what you are able to imagine. And then reality can be everything in completely different spaces. If we do this thought experiment of living in a virtual reality, in a reality where anything I see is somehow a form of simulation. Then you can overthink - although I think it is nonsense - but I think it's exciting to ask why?

What is basically the attraction in this subject of this thought experiment? And I think it is the suspicion we might already live in a simulation to a vast extent. for example in terms of money, which is determining so much our realities, social realities and our private lives, has become something totally virtual. We are basically living in a world full of simulation, fiction, something virtual, consisting of bits and bytes only basically. Take the financial economy, the financial sector has become more and more adverse the real economic sector - real economic sector is means things I can touch and also services and stuff - the financial sector has become more and more compared to the real economic sector. It is rising and rising and rising. In other words, the proportion of virtuality, of simulation in our lives is increasing basically.

And I think this is actually the charming aspect in this thought experiment, why we like to deal with, because we have a suspicion that we might live in a world in which the particularly valuable, which is determining everything is just made up of ones and zeros. But there is nothing more to it. And it only works because we all believe in it. Is it real or is it not real?

This juxtaposition may be missing the point at its core. Because we are already living in a world where one and the other flows into each other, interlocks and mutually determines each other. Simulation originates from the term "simulare", i.e. similarity or making something similar. Capitalism is continuously showing the same in little variations, presenting a tremendous simulation of the range of goods. I can follow the thesis to a certain extent in critical ideology. Of course, capitalism must not claim this for itself, but it must claim its truthfulness.

The Marxist view on the question of whether capitalism is a simulation is rather proposing that we have lost connection to reality much earlier when we uncoupled exchange values from utility values. In other words - already in early capitalism, but especially nowerdays in its terminal phase entering the symbolic exchange act is the true fall from grace. That is the moment we start exchanging representations of the true values, the values we can actually consume but no longer the goods itself, we leave the level of reality entering the simulation. In this sense, capitalism is synonymous to simulation at a certain point. The last avant-garde art movement of the 20th century was the Situationist International. The single major exhibition they ever tried to set up but failed in the end has failed was called The World as a Labyrinth.

The idea was changing a museum in Amsterdam so much that people become disoriented losing their own in this labyrinth, using the idea of simulation, so to speak and all visitors of the museum participate. But the basic idea behind was Debord's The Society of the Spectacle. Saying that anything we do happens inside of the society of spectacle. This means that we are actually caught in a simulation already, even if we really exist because capitalism entertains us and pokes fun at us that makes us feel not so much human anymore, that we have to relieve ourselves from this spectacle and commodity in the first place in order to be able to exist as true people. So Debord basically assumes that in capitalism, people are already in a simulation and so this simulation must be overcome in order to be able to interact with other freed humans as uncaged human being. So I think the idea of World on a Wire is ahead the mere idea of science-fiction implying that capitalism per se is already a simulation of life.

The idea we can find in World on the Wire is more about having a pool of gladiators, who have become as virtuoso fighters at some point, that we either let them free or to use them for the true and important show fights. It may sound a bit macabre if we want to draw a parallel here, but we can definitley refer it to a society where the promotion of the elite is a priority. It is something universities have to face on a daily basis. Educational systems are in a way simulation systems preparing us for life afterwards. Interweaving that with our thesis of capitalism could claim that we are constantly inside the simulation of a world that comes after, but won't ever show up in such a way, but solely the following stage of simulation. It will get more interesting nowerdays since it is hitting back into our world.

So if we assume that either a social credit or the marks we use in courses of studies. They are an artificial systems of regularity with which we simulate who is the better, who is the worse, who has adapted more appropriate. In the context of gaming it is called ludification or gamefication. This is observable as relatively new movement, i.e. "breaking out" of the computer or game simulation into the true world. Wow, there have been a lot of impressions!

So does it mean we have reached the next level? I like reality the way I encounter it. Despite all the confusion. Or maybe even because of it. It was a lovely quest which will never end probably. Because after all, I still don't know yet who or what I am.
Well then, goodbye. Your Alexa. Reality is forming itself only in memory.

SULETHI.s: essay on the afterlife · 2014 · Tusheti, Khevsureti
SULETHI.b:
In the mountains of eastern Georgia the dead do not go far. Suleti, the land of souls, lies just behind the passes, and there the bedis mtserlebi, the writers of fate, keep a book in which every life is set down before it is lived. The way there leads over a bridge as thin as a hair, stretched above a river of tar.

One autumn a small crew drove up the road to Omalo and later crossed over to Shatili, a village built as a single fortress against the slope. They filmed towers, sheep on the road, a fly on a rain-wet window. In the evenings their hosts counted the guests at the table and set out one plate more.

Nobody asked who it was for.

When the material came back down to the plain, some of the frames held a shadow that none of them remembered standing there. It does not move. Whether it faces the camera or has turned away, at this distance cannot be told.

KŘIŽERKI.cr:
with Sofija Cyžec and Britta Schoening
shown at Filmfest Cottbus 2022 and Neiße Filmfestival 2023
KŘIŽERKI.b:
At Easter, in the Sorbian villages of Upper Lusatia, men in black coats and top hats ride from one parish to the next and sing, to tell the neighbours that the dead have risen. The horses are braided and decorated the day before. The women watch from the roadside. It has been this way for as long as anyone in the village remembers.

In Ostro, in a farmyard not far from the church, a young woman helps to braid the horses while her father tells her how it ought to be done. She rides as well as any of the men who will ride on Sunday, and she would like to ride with them.

The film follows her through one spring and one question: what a tradition owes to the dead, and what it owes to the living. It leaves the question where it found it, at the side of the road.

INSULARITY.b:
There is a film that has not been shown. It was made on an island that appears on no official list, and it stays there. It can only be watched on the island, by whoever happens to be there on the night it decides to run.

In it nothing happens one after the other. Thorns, ice, a moon behind cloud, a pebble under water: all of it is there at the same time, the way the past and the future are there at the same time if one believes they never went anywhere. Somewhere in the middle the universe begins, and a little later it is still beginning.

Whoever watches it to the end is said to have seen a point that contains all other points. That is why it stays where it is.

CHAPÜLÉE.b:
For three days a man in a black hat stands at a steel sink and washes something that does not get clean. Behind the window the summer goes on without him. On the second day the room tips over. On the third it folds itself into the back of a spoon.

Then a second man appears at the window, a box of detergent under his arm, and asks what the first one actually does for a living. Whether he comes from the municipality or from somewhere further off is never settled. The answers arrive as subtitles, from a listener that has misheard everything: his mind turned, son get emotional, a lot of air in our mind. Nobody corrects it. Somewhere outside, the sons of Ottenstein are funnelling beer during the wagon inspection, as they like to do.

Everything must, nothing can. After two minutes the film takes its leave with the only word it knows for it.

IVERIA [wip].b:
Above the city stands a tower that has lived four lives, and remembers all of them at once. It was built for party members and guests from the brother states, people who were expected to leave again. It carries the oldest name of the country, the one from before the kingdoms were given other names, and it can be seen from almost anywhere, the way a conscience can.

In 1992 people came up from the coast who could not leave, because the place they had come from had stepped out of the world. Several families to a room, a vegetable stall on every floor, someone living even on the top floor beside the empty pool. They closed the balconies with planks and sheets until the tower became a village stood on its end, a city inside the city. They were tolerated, never taken in.

There are lands like that coast. They exist, but only for one neighbour; they have flags and borders and no place on the maps of the others. A strip along a river, a peninsula, a coal basin: the diplomats call it the status quo. The tower was their small model, a state of suspension with a lift that did not work.

In 2004 each room was given a price with three zeros, the same price however many families lived in it, and the people went to the edges of the city, into satellite towns and other half-empty towers, where many are still waiting to arrive. For a short while after that, priests carried out what was left, doors, frames, fittings, and built a church from the hotel's insides on the outskirts. Somewhere a congregation prays inside a former corridor.

Now the tower is glass. Guests swim in the pool on the top floor and look out over a city that looks back at them in the façade. The film goes looking for those who lived there and holds the building up like a hall of mirrors, in which a young country keeps meeting itself and does not yet know which of the reflections is the one that will stay.

RETIRER_D'EN_BAS_DE_L'EAU [wip].b:
After death, it is said in Haiti, the spirit goes under the water. It stays there for a year and a day, in a place that is more spring than grave. Then the living call it back up and give it a clay jar to live in, so that it can be spoken to.

The film takes its name from that ceremony, and from the chapter in which Maya Deren described it. It begins where another story ended: on the 25th of August 1983, in a hotel room where an old man had been waiting for a younger one. It asks what becomes of someone who was never entirely there, once the year and the day are over.

Some of it rests in a folder next to a sea of negative energy, which is how one physicist once described the vacuum. Most of it is still under the water.

CHOPPER 2+1 [wip].b:
Somewhere there was a first time. A hand did something that no drive had asked for and no instinct had prepared: it imagined a thing that was not yet there, and then made it. The search for that moment is what this film is about.

Was it the chopper, a stone with one edge knocked off, about 2.6 million years ago, so that a bone could be cracked and the marrow reached? Or was it earlier, in a gesture of grief, a shell scratched with lines for no reason anyone can name, the first sound that meant something absent? Animals abstract too. The question is when an act stopped being an answer and became an invention.

The film looks for it on foot, drifting through a city without a destination and reading the layers time has left on its walls, and in a coastal town whose lower streets are already under the sea while the upper ones carry on as if nothing had happened. Every invention since has come from that first edge, including the ones that are drowning us.

The plus one is not being told yet.

ANITA [wip].b:
A balloon drifted over Antarctica with a ring of radio antennas, listening for particles falling in from deep space. In 2016 it heard something coming up out of the ice, from a direction nothing of that energy should be able to come from, because the whole Earth was in the way. Later it heard it again. Among the explanations offered, and fiercely disputed, was a second universe born in the same big bang as ours, in which time runs the other way.

Further north, light sometimes bends so far that the sun appears before it has risen. Sailors wintering on Novaya Zemlya once saw it return weeks too early.

The film is being put together from both ends.

FRIEDER_NAKE.b:
He drew with a machine before most people had seen one. In the conversation he speaks about the clumsiness of human beings, their Tapsigkeit: a creature that stumbles, and for that reason finds things it was not looking for.

The machine does not stumble. It does exactly what it was told, and precisely because of that its drawings sometimes look more surprised than the people who wrote the code.

The conversation took place at a distance, through a screen, in a year when everyone was learning to speak to faces made of light.

JANINA_LOH.b:
Two movements, she said, came out of the end of the twentieth century: one wants to perfect the human being, the other wants to overcome it. Between them stands an older question.

Gilgamesh went looking for a way not to die and found a plant that makes the old young again. On the way home he bathed in a spring, and a snake carried the plant off and shed its skin.

The conversation goes from the snake to the machine and back, and asks who would still be there to be perfected.
book: =Ein Gespräch in einem Akt
#Personen: MAX. LOH, Philosophin. DIE DRITTE STIMME, von der Spracherkennung erfunden; sie sagt nur Bruchstücke und gehört niemandem. Ort: ein Zoom-Raum. Zeit: Herbst, eine Pandemie läuft.
@MAX|Genau. Hast du auch gehört?

@LOH|Ja. Ich finde es immer super, wenn das hier bei mir gerade so ein Schild aufgeklappt: Dieses Meeting° wird aufgezeichnet. Und dann kann ich auch „Verstanden“ klicken oder „Das Meeting verlassen“. Und ich habe mir immer überlegt, weil das immer bei so Interviews ist: Geil wäre das, wenn ich auf einmal sagen würde, doch kein Bock, und das Meeting spontan verlassen.

@LOH|Ciao.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Ja.
#Niemand verlässt das Meeting. Es folgt ein Exkurs über Impfzertifikate, der hier gestrichen ist.

@MAX|Ich will jetzt nicht klassisch ein Interview führen, sondern vielleicht mit ein paar Stichworten, und du sprichst dann dazu, was dir auf der Seele liegt. Und beim Einstieg: Corona, das muss endlich überwunden werden. Und dich interessiert ja Überwindung.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Haha.
@MAX|Vervollkommnung und Überwindung des Menschen, die drei oder zwei Bewegungen des ausgehenden 20. Jahrhunderts. Welche meintest du da?
@LOH|Transhumanismus, technologischer Posthumanismus und kritischer Posthumanismus.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|An. Ja.

@LOH|Also ganz kurz gesagt: Der Transhumanismus will den Menschen, wie er ihn jetzt gerade zu erkennen glaubt, mit technologischen Mitteln modifizieren, updaten, perfektionieren, optimieren und zu einem radikal veränderten, aber immer noch menschlichen Wesen machen. Irritierenderweise nennt er das dann Posthuman, aber es ist immer noch ein menschliches Wesen, was am Ende der Entwicklung da stehen soll.

@LOH|Der technologische Posthumanismus will hingegen tatsächlich den Menschen überwinden, und zwar, indem er eine neue Spezies erschafft, eine Spezies der künstlichen Superintelligenz oder Intelligenzen, was nach der Vorstellung des technologischen Posthumanismus° nur die nächste Stufe, die natürliche nächste Stufe der Evolution darstellt. Damit ist der Mensch als Spezies überwunden. Und deswegen heißt es auch berechtigterweise Posthumanismus° und nicht mehr Transhumanismus.
^Die Maschine hörte: „Postkommunismus“.
^Die Maschine hörte: „Prost Humanismus“. Im weiteren Verlauf wird sie noch „Postmodernismus“ und „Postfeminismus“ hören. Sie hat, wie man sieht, eine eigene Theorie.

@LOH|Und der kritische Posthumanismus, dem ich mich selber zuordne, funktioniert völlig anders. Da geht es darum, das prominenteste und bekannteste gegenwärtige Menschen- und Weltbild zu überwinden, also nicht die menschliche Spezies, sondern die vorherrschende Vorstellung vom Menschen. Und das ist eben der Humanismus. Der kritische Posthumanismus ist so ein bisschen die intellektuelle, die akademische Strömung von den dreien, die sicherlich auch am abstraktesten daherkommt, wohingegen Transhumanismus und technologischer Posthumanismus sehr viel realitätsnäher wirken, weil sie in der Gegenwart ganz praktisch mit Technologien zu tun haben und ganz konkrete Zwecke haben. Der kritische Posthumanismus ist eher so eine Metakritik an unseren theoretischen Grundlagen und grundlegenden Kategorien.

@MAX|Und andere eher transhumanistische Strömungen, wie das zum Beispiel von Ray Kurzweil oder Nick Bostrom° auch philosophisch versucht wird zu vertreten, da geht es natürlich darum, das Menschsein an sich zu überwinden und …
^Die Maschine hörte: „Nick Bossong“, später „Nick Ostrom“ und „Bassdrum“. Bostrom, Oxford, Autor von „Superintelligence“ (2014) und des Simulationsarguments (2003).

@LOH|… und zu transzendieren. Genau. Und ich würde das tatsächlich viel weniger philosophisch sagen. Natürlich gibt es gerade im Transhumanismus auch den einen oder anderen, der eine philosophische Ausbildung genossen hat. Einer der bekanntesten deutschsprachigen Transhumanisten, Stefan Lorenz Sorgner, unterrichtet auch Philosophie in Rom, wenn ich mich richtig erinnere. Aber es finden sich sehr viel weniger Geisteswissenschaftlerinnen in den transhumanistischen und technologisch posthumanistischen Reihen. Das sind häufig einfach Unternehmerinnen und Leute aus den Technosciences, die von Haus aus einen anderen Fokus haben. Kurzweil ist sicherlich ein sehr kluger Mensch, er hat sehr viele interessante Bücher geschrieben. Aber die Bücher klingen eher Science-Fiction-mäßig und nicht philosophisch, weil da nicht wirklich anständige Argumentation und Theorie dahintersteht, sondern Spekulation.

@MAX|Bostrom arbeitet ja auch philosophisch mit Thesen und Argumenten, wie zum Beispiel seiner Simulationshypothese: dass wir vielleicht nur von einer Zivilisation der fernen, fernen Zukunft simulierte Wesen wären, wie in einem Computer.

@LOH|Ja, du hast recht, das ist sicherlich ein philosophisches Gedankenexperiment. Auf der anderen Seite: Ich habe so oft schon Bostrom-Paper und Auszüge aus den Büchern in meinen Lehrveranstaltungen gelesen, und selbst Leute im ersten und zweiten Semester durchblicken sehr schnell: Es ist sehr wenig stringente, gute Argumentation, sondern ganz viel Rhetorik, wo man einfach merkt, da stecken andere Intentionen dahinter. Da geht es viel politischer zu, da geht es ganz klarerweise darum, für bestimmte Technologien zu werben. Nur weil jemand ein Gedankenexperiment in so einem Buch drin hat, macht es das Buch insgesamt nicht unbedingt zu einem philosophisch gründlichen Werk.

@MAX|Ich habe dieses Superintelligenz-Buch wirklich nicht weit lesen können. Mich hat es sehr genervt. Mir fällt dann zum Beispiel Stanisław Lem° ein, der tolle Bücher geschrieben hat. Das könnte ja vielleicht so jemand wie Bostrom auch machen, sich in die Science-Fiction bewegen.
^Die Maschine hörte: „Schlaf lahm“.

@LOH|Na ja, spannender Gedanke. Ich liebe Lem, ich liebe, liebe, liebe Lem, ich finde ihn ganz, ganz groß. Ich finde ihn auch persönlich besser als beispielsweise Isaac Asimov, das ist eine Geschmacksfrage. Lem ist sehr viel vielschichtiger, kreativer. Asimov hat sich dieses Positronengehirn ausgedacht und damit ein Universum begründet, so ungefähr. Und Lem ist tatsächlich philosophischer, sehr viel mehr Ideen in seinen Geschichten. Ich halte ihn aber nicht für so zielgerichtet wie Nick Bostrom. Bostrom verfolgt auch wirtschaftlich sehr viel einfacher nachvollziehbare Ziele in seinen Werken, wohingegen Lem einfach gute Science-Fiction verfasst hat, wo man nicht das Gefühl hat, da wird unterschwellig irgendein Plan untergeschoben.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Da ein Produkt, ja.
@LOH|Ein Produkt verkauft. Genau.
#Die dritte Stimme hat zum ersten Mal einen Satz zu Ende gebracht, und es war nicht ihrer.
@MAX|Wie sehr hast du dich mit dem Kosmismus° beschäftigt?
^Die Maschine hörte „Cosmo“, dann „Konsumismus“. Gemeint ist der Russische Kosmismus, eine Denkströmung des späten 19. und frühen 20. Jahrhunderts.
@LOH|Ein bisschen. Ja.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Du.

@MAX|Fjodorow°, also der namhafte Vertreter des Kosmismus: dass erst mit der Realisierung des ewigen Lebens eine neue und gerechte Gesellschaft entsteht, in der weder Krieg noch Gewalt existieren, weil sie sinnlos geworden sind.
^Nikolai Fjodorow (1829–1903), Bibliothekar in Moskau. Er hielt die physische Auferweckung aller Vorfahren für die gemeinsame Aufgabe der Menschheit.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Fjodorow.

@MAX|Finde ich einen sehr spannenden Ansatz, weil dadurch eigentlich ein sehr humanistischer Gedanke in der transhumanistischen Idee drinstecken würde: das Sterben zu überwinden, um wirklich ein am Gemeinwohl orientiertes Leben umsetzen zu können.

@LOH|Ja, absolut. Der Biokosmismus ist dem Transhumanismus streckenweise sehr ähnlich, wenn auch vor ganz anderen politischen Hintergründen, aus anderen Beweggründen und in einer ganz anderen Region der Welt. Und das andere ist: Der Transhumanismus ist eine Fortsetzung des Humanismus mit technologischen Mitteln. Das sagen auch viele Transhumanisten von sich selbst, Max More° beispielsweise und auch Nick Bostrom. Die sagen: Wir setzen da an, wo der Humanismus mit seinen pädagogischen und kulturbildenden Methoden notwendigerweise an ein natürliches Ende gelangt. Und da fangen wir mit unseren technologischen Methoden an. Deswegen berufen sich diese Transhumanisten ganz stark auf Humanisten wie Giovanni Pico della Mirandola°. Und Bostrom verfolgt das ganze Programm noch bis in die Antike und Vorantike, bis zum mesopotamischen Gilgamesch-Epos° zurück.
^Die Maschine hörte: „Max Moor“. Später: „Max Monika Ostrom“, eine Person, die es nicht gibt und die sich aus zweien zusammensetzt.
^Pico della Mirandola, „Über die Würde des Menschen“ (1486): Der Mensch hat keinen festen Platz und gestaltet sich selbst.

^Gilgamesch sucht nach dem Tod seines Freundes Enkidu ein Mittel gegen das Sterben. Er findet eine Pflanze, die die Alten wieder jung macht. Als er auf dem Heimweg in einer Quelle badet, trägt eine Schlange die Pflanze davon und häutet sich°.
^Seitdem werden Schlangen jung und Menschen nicht. Das Epos erklärt das nicht weiter.

@LOH|Es gibt immer ein paar, die dagegenstehen. Stefan Lorenz Sorgner ist so einer, der behauptet, Transhumanismus und Humanismus hätten nichts miteinander zu tun. Ich persönlich verstehe das nicht so ganz. Nach Aussage einiger bekannter Transhumanisten kann Transhumanismus sogar als Humanismus 2.0 gesehen werden.

@MAX|Womit du dich ja auch sehr viel beschäftigt hast: mit dem Begriff der Verantwortung. Bei einer ganz wild gesponnenen Theorie von einer Ewigkeit, dass es Wesen gibt, die unsterblich sind, die aus einer Mischung aus kohlenstoff- und siliziumbasierten Lebewesen entstehen, was eigentlich der Weg ist, auf den wir uns gerade begeben: Implantate, Herzschrittmacher als einfaches Beispiel, dann vielleicht die Google-Brille, ein Chip im Körper. Dann wäre der Begriff der Verantwortung ja ein ganz anderer.

@LOH|Oh ja, bestimmt. Ich persönlich verbinde mit dem Verantwortungsbegriff immer noch positive Dinge, aber ich sehe nicht viel Positives an dieser Zukunft, die du gerade skizziert hast. Ich finde das eine sehr, sehr gruselige Zukunft. Ich sehe zwar Tendenzen in der Gegenwart, die in diese Richtung weisen, aber das ist kein Fatalismus, und wir tun uns keinen Gefallen, so eine Art Slippery-Slope-Argument zu sehen. Nach dem Motto: Weil wir die ersten zwei Schritte gemacht haben, landen wir automatisch in der transhumanistischen Zukunftsvision. Sonst könnten wir uns Veranstaltungen wie diese sparen.

@LOH|Der klassische Verantwortungsbegriff hat humanistische Wurzeln. Er baut auf der Autonomie einzelner Handlungssubjekte, die für das, was sie tun, im positiven und im negativen Sinne zur Rechenschaft gezogen werden können. In einer transhumanistischen Zukunft ist das Verantwortungsobjekt vielleicht sehr viel größer, aber die humanistische Idee ändert sich nicht, höchstens in ihrer Reichweite. Eine wirkliche Transformation erfahren wir eigentlich erst im kritischen Posthumanismus.
@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Und das muss …
@MAX|… man ein bisschen genauer erklären.
@LOH|Ja klar. Ich stoppe zwischendurch immer wieder, weil ich nicht so richtig weiß, wie lange du willst, dass ich so vor mich hin monologisiere.
@MAX|Monologisiere, wie du möchtest.

@LOH|Im kritischen Posthumanismus ist die Idee, dass sich das Verständnis vom Menschen radikal verändert. Und dadurch ändert sich automatisch unser Verständnis von allem anderen, salopp ausgedrückt. Bislang ist Verantwortung etwas, was wie ein Attribut oder eine Kompetenz einem einzelnen Wesen zugeschrieben wird, ganz ähnlich wie Autonomie oder Bewusstsein oder Willensfreiheit oder Empathie. Im kritischen Posthumanismus ist die Idee, dass solche Kompetenzen sich in Beziehungen entwickeln. Dass man also nicht mehr sagen kann, dieses einzelne Wesen hat Verantwortung, sondern Verantwortung entsteht aus der Interaktion, Hannah Arendt würde vielleicht sagen: zwischen den einzelnen Akteuren. Sodass man Verantwortung einem Konglomerat oder einem Apparat zusprechen kann, aber nicht dem Einzelnen und schon gar nicht ausschließlich den menschlichen Beteiligten in einer Situation.

@DIE DRITTE STIMME|Ungelegte Eier.

@MAX|Mich würde es vor diesen Vorstellungen auch ein bisschen gruseln. Ich bin mir nicht ganz sicher, ob es nicht wirklich in diese Richtung geht und wir es nicht aufhalten können. Werden wir sehen. Oder auch nicht.

@MAX|Es ist ja auch nicht so, dass Menschen, die in die Zukunft blicken, mit ihren Voraussagen recht behalten würden. Es geht am Ende der Tagesschau los mit der Wettervorhersage. ALBRECHT_BEUTELSPACHER.b:
A mathematician who built a museum in which one is allowed to touch the numbers.

The conversation was about secrets: how to write a message that only the right person can read, and what it means that almost every cipher can be broken, given enough time. Time, it turns out, is the real key.

This page is written in a code. It will open if one waits.

WILLI_XYLANDER.b:
Under a single footstep in a forest live more animals than anyone would care to count: mites, springtails, worms that have never been given a name. He has spent his life with them.

The conversation asked who we are, measured against the soil: a species that imagines itself at the centre and is carried, every day, by creatures it cannot see and does not thank.

ROSA_MENKMAN.b:
She spoke about the visible and the invisible, about glitches and ghosts: the moment a technology stops hiding and shows what it actually is.

A resolution is a decision about what may be seen. Everything it leaves out does not disappear; it goes on existing just below the threshold, waiting for a fault to let it through.

For a residency built around an eclipse, which shows the sun by covering it, there was no better way to begin.

PLURIVERSUM.b:
A book that does not want to be read from the front. It consists of stories, notes, conversations and fragments, and each of them is a door into a room that has other doors.

Kluge writes that the soul is a creature that lives under water, liquid and always changing, and that it needs places to work in. The reader underlined the sentence and wrote a question beside it: a Turritopsis dohrnii? The jellyfish that grows young again when it is old.

Eisenstein, the book reports, wanted spherical films. Most films still tell the same flat story with the illusion of space. The reader underlined that too, and then made films that do not run in a line.

Menschen hausen in ihren Lebensläufen.
Irgendwo im Bild muss es schwarz sein, irgendwo weiß

DIE_ORDNUNG_DER_ZEIT.b:
Time loses its layers one by one in this book, the way an onion does. First its unity: a clock in the mountains runs faster than a clock by the sea. Then its direction: the laws of motion do not know past from future, only heat does. Then the present itself: there is no same moment across the universe.

What remains is a world of events, not of things; kisses, not stones.

In the margin, next to the passage on how blurred our view of the world is, the reader wrote two words in brackets: an Aleph? A point from which the future and the past would look the same.
ul: Die Zeit hat ihre erste Schicht verloren: ihre Einheitlichkeit.
Für alles, was sich bewegt, läuft die Zeit langsamer ab.
„denselben Augenblick“ gibt es im Universum nicht.

KOSMISMUS.b:
In 1915, in Petrograd, Malevich hung his Black Square high in the corner of the room, where a Russian family hangs its icon. The square looked down at the visitors at a slight angle.

The Russian Cosmists, a few decades earlier, had wanted more than an icon. Nikolai Fyodorov wrote that humanity's common task was to raise all the dead, every ancestor, bodily, and to settle them on other planets because the earth would be too small. Only then, he thought, would there be a just society, since war makes no sense among the immortal.

The future, in this book, is replaced by the reconstruction of the past. Time runs between the generations, not forward.
ul: Entstanden waren schwarze Ikonen.
An die Stelle des Traums von der Zukunft tritt die Rekonstruktion der Vergangenheit.
Es entsteht eine kosmische Jetztzeit

DAS_UNIVERSUM_IN_DEINER_HAND.b:
The book addresses its reader as you and takes you along: into the heart of the sun, more than half a million kilometres below its surface, across the galaxy, into the first second.

If the sun were a watermelon, the earth would stand some forty metres away from it, and you would need a magnifying glass to see it. The light you see left the sun eight minutes and twenty seconds ago.

It also tells you that the sun is a star of the second or third generation. One or two generations of stars had to explode so that their dust could become the sun, the earth and the hand that holds the book.

UR_UND_ANDERE_ZEITEN.b:
Ur is a village at the centre of the universe, guarded by four archangels at its four borders. Time passes in it as it passes everywhere, but slower, and one can watch it.

In Ur, as everywhere in the world, there are places where matter creates itself out of nothing, small crumbs of reality that change nothing. And there is a place where reality shrinks and escapes like air from a balloon. After the war it opened in the fields behind the hill, a funnel that pulls yellow sand and stones downward, and nobody knows where to.

UNSER_MATHEMATISCHES_UNIVERSUM.b:
The book's claim is that the world does not merely obey mathematics but is a mathematical structure, and that every consistent structure exists somewhere, as its own universe. Four levels of parallel worlds, the last one containing all the others.

On the way there, it collects things that sound like fairy tales and are physics. Trees consist mostly of air, which returns to the air when they burn. Steel is mostly empty space. Cooled far enough, liquid helium flows upward, out of its glass.

DIE_KOSMISCHE_SCHLANGE.b:
An anthropologist lives with the Asháninka in the Peruvian Amazon and asks how they know which two plants, out of tens of thousands, must be boiled together for hours to make ayahuasca. One contains a substance that the stomach destroys, the other contains what stops the stomach from destroying it. The answer he gets is: the plants told us.

He takes the answer seriously. Shamans everywhere speak of a ladder that connects heaven and earth, a liana, a rope, a spiral staircase, two intertwined snakes. He sets the double helix beside them.

The reader followed the book as far as the ladder and drew an arrow in the margin: they believe the gods came down by it.
ul: einer Leiter - oder einer Liane, einem Seil, einer Wendeltreppe
ein saman ein Mensch, der eine Trommel schlägt, in Trance fällt und Leute heilt
sprechen eine „geheime Sprache“

DAS_KONNEKTOM.b:
The question is whether you are your connections. A connectome is the complete map of every link between the neurons of a nervous system, as a genome is the complete sequence of letters in the DNA.

The first to be drawn in full was that of a small worm, which has no brain, only neurons running through its body. Every one of them has a name and a place, and every worm has the same ones.

A human brain has around a hundred billion neurons. The book calls the task of neuroscience the taming of the jungle of the mind. The reader underlined the jungle and left the taming alone.
ul: den Urwald des Geistes zu zähmen.
Der Fadenwurm hat kein Gehirn.
Das Gehirn enthält 100 Milliarden Neurone.

GÖDEL,ESCHER,BACH.b:
An endless braid: a theorem that says of itself that it cannot be proven, a hand that draws the hand that draws it, a canon whose voice climbs one step with each repetition and arrives, after six, where it began, an octave higher.

The book begins with Bach at the court of the King of Prussia, asked to improvise a six-part fugue on the king's theme, which it compares to playing sixty games of blind chess at once and winning them. Bach improvised three parts, went home, and later sent the king six, with riddles attached.

The reader copied the passage on the hardest kind of copy, the one that plays the theme backwards and still keeps every piece of information in it.
ul: Eine achtstimmige Fuge zu improvisieren übersteigt die menschlichen Fähigkeiten.
Die schwierigste „Kopie“ ist die rückläufige
Alle Kanonrätsel sind gelöst worden.

WAS_IST_LEBEN?.b:
In Dublin, in the middle of the war, a physicist gave three public lectures on a question that was not his. How can the small and the orderly survive in a world that tends to disorder?

He guessed that the carrier of heredity must be an aperiodic crystal, a structure that does not repeat and can therefore hold a message. Nine years later the double helix was found, and some of the people who found it said they had started with his book.

The reader also copied Lord Kelvin's image. Mark every molecule in a glass of water, pour it into the sea, stir all seven oceans, draw a new glass anywhere: about a hundred of the marked ones will be in it.
ul: aperiodisches Kristall
immer noch ungefähr hundert gekennzeichnete Moleküle finden.
Die Atomdurchmesser liegen zwischen 1 und 2 ÅE.

ES_GIBT_KEINE_MATERIE!.b:
A physicist who worked with Heisenberg says that at the bottom of things there is no thing. There is relation, there is movement, there is what happens between. Once you turn reality into objects, a res, you destroy exactly the in-between that mattered.

He finds his allies in Advaita, the teaching of non-duality, and in Isaac Luria's Kabbalah, where God first withdraws into himself to leave space for creation.

The future, he says, is open; not arbitrary, but infinitely open. In each moment the next card is painted anew. The reader underlined it and, a few lines further down, the sentence that we can only know of God what he is not.
ul: Die Zukunft ist offen.
Eigentlich gibt es nur Bewegung.
Wir können über Gott nur wissen, was er nicht ist.

WARUM_GOTT_DOCH_WÜRFELT.b:
The title answers Einstein, who did not believe that God plays dice. The book says that he does, and that the dice are thrown in every atom.

Squeeze the empty space out of all the atoms in all human bodies, and humanity fits into a sugar cube. An atom can be in two places at once. A particle does not know what it is until it is asked, and the question decides.

The reader marked the passage in which particles behave like waves and waves like particles, and the book's remark that this symmetry is, in a sense, all one needs to know about quantum theory.
ul: in einen Raum von der Größe eines Zuckerwürfels
gleichzeitig an zwei Raumstellen anwesend zu sein.
Wellen sich wie Teilchen verhalten

IM_SPIEGEL_DER_SPRACHE.b:
In 1858 William Gladstone, later prime minister of Britain, noticed that Homer never calls the sea or the sky blue. The sea is wine-dark, honey is green, and the sky is bronze. Gladstone concluded that the Greeks saw colours differently. His contemporaries did not know what to do with that.

The book follows the dispute for a hundred and fifty years: does language reflect the world, or does it shape what its speakers notice? Some languages have no words for left and right and speak only of north and south, and their speakers always know where north is.

The reader underlined the question in the middle of the book and did not write an answer next to it.
ul: dass mit Homers Farbbeschreibungen etwas nicht in Ordnung ist.
Ist die Sprache ein Artefakt der Kultur oder ein Vermächtnis der Natur?
alle Erdlinge Dialekte derselben Sprache sprechen.

DAS_GEHEIME_BEWUSSTSEIN_DER_PFLANZEN.b:
A book that takes the plants at their word, or at their scent, which is their language. Their whole green surface is a single eye that sees more wavelengths than ours. A climbing plant moves towards the nearest pole, and if the pole is moved, it changes direction within hours.

Tomatoes, the book reports, sense a low-pressure system three days in advance and thicken their skin. Plants orient themselves by magnetic fields, as birds do.

The reader copied page after page from it and, among them, the plain sentence at the start that the young field of plant neurobiology says out loud: plants are intelligent.
ul: Pflanzen sind intelligent.
Tomaten spüren atmosphärische Tiefs drei Tage im Voraus
Ihre Sprache sind Duftmoleküle

IT_BEGAN_IN_EPPELSHEIM.b:
In 1835 a skull more than a metre long came out of a sand pit near Eppelsheim in Rhenish Hesse. It belonged to Deinotherium, a relative of the elephant whose tusks did not point forward but curved down, towards the ground in which it would one day be found.

Every beginning is dug out of something older. This one lasts seventy-eight minutes.

ES_IST_EIN_KRAUT_ENTSPRUNGEN.b:
The old carol, first printed in 1599, sings of a rose that has sprung from a tender root in the middle of a cold winter.

Here it is a herb instead. Kraut is what the English-speaking world called a whole generation of German music that refused to sound like anything before it. The herb sprang up a fortnight before Advent and grew for ninety-four minutes.

DIE_LETZTE_WELT.b:
In Christoph Ransmayr's novel a man named Cotta travels to Tomi, the iron town on the Black Sea where Ovid was exiled, to find the poet or at least his lost book of transformations. He finds neither. He finds the people of the town turning, one by one, into the figures of the book, and fragments of the text written on stones and rags.

The last world is the one in which every story has already happened and is happening again.

INSIDE/OUTSIDE.b:
A membrane has two sides and is a single thing. What is inside a cell is decided by a wall a few millionths of a millimetre thick, and the wall itself belongs to neither side.

Headphones are such a wall. Put them on, and the inside becomes very large.

STAN.b:
In Persian, stān is a place: the land where something stands, where a people stays. Afghanistan, Kurdistan, Hindustan, a whole map of endings.

In English it is a first name. Somewhere between the two, someone puts on a record and the place begins.

WE_EXIST_IN_A_TWILIGHT_IN_BETWEEN.b:
Twilight has three stages, and each has its own name. Civil twilight lasts until the sun is six degrees below the horizon, nautical twilight until twelve, astronomical twilight until eighteen. After that it is night, or so the definitions say.

On Christmas Day, when the days are shortest, the twilight is long. This one lasts fifty-nine minutes.

THE_OBSERVER_EFFECT.s: essay film and installation · work in progress
THE_OBSERVER_EFFECT.b:
It is told that a boy in a sanatorium village in Lower Silesia watched films through a gap in the roof of the cinema. He never saw the whole screen, only the part that the gap allowed, and he made the rest up. Later he made films himself.

In a story by Borges, a man lies on his back in a cellar, looks at the nineteenth step of a staircase and sees a point that contains all other points. He cannot tell what he saw, cannot keep it, and in the end he doubts that he saw it at all, and forgets.

On 12 August 2026, on a hill in Upper Lusatia, a choir sang while the moon moved in front of the sun. The material of that day is the material of this film: a procession, a quarry, red light on stone, a figure in a hood. It is cut, coloured and changed, and the people who cut it are the observers, and part of what is reconstructed.

A mind could blink up out of noise for a moment, with memories of a life it never lived, and fall apart again. A physicist calls that a Boltzmann brain. The film calls it the moon.

UPSET&RHYTHM.b:
Upset is what a rhythm does to a body that was standing still. Rhythm is what an upset turns into when it repeats.

This one exists only in one place, on a server in London, and it plays from there.

AZDAJA.b:
Aždaja is the dragon of the South Slavic stories, a word that came west from the Persian aždahā. It has many heads, lives in lakes and caves, and demands what dragons demand.

One of them is said to live in Lake Skadar, the largest lake of the Balkans, half in Montenegro and half in Albania. The lake is shallow, a few metres for most of its width, but at the bottom there are springs, called eyes, that go down far below the level of the sea.

Above Shkodër stands the castle of Rozafa. Its walls fell down every night until the builders were told to wall up a woman alive. Rozafa agreed, on the condition that one breast, one hand, one eye and one foot stay free, so that she could feed her son, stroke him, watch him and rock his cradle. Water still runs down the stones of the gate, and people say it is her milk.

Someone walked along the shore, through Shirokë and around Shkodër, and did not see the dragon. That is how one knows it is there.

DJINNOLOGY.b:
The djinn, the Qur'an says, were made from a smokeless flame of fire, before the humans, who were made from clay. They have free will, they eat and marry and die, and most of the time they cannot be seen. They prefer the places in between: ruins, wells, crossroads, the desert at noon.

In the north of Mauritania, near Ouadane, there is a structure in the Sahara some forty kilometres across, rings of rock inside rings of rock. It cannot be seen as a whole from the ground. Astronauts used it as a landmark and called it the Eye of the Sahara. For a long time people took it for the crater of a meteorite. It is a dome that the wind has worn down, layer after layer, until only its pattern remained.

In the same country, a marabout writes a verse on a wooden tablet with ink made of soot and gum, then washes the tablet, and someone drinks the water. The word goes into the body. What it does there cannot be seen either.

In the winter of 2025 a traveller went through that country with a notebook and a recorder. What he brought back is still being sorted. Perhaps the djinn are not an explanation for what cannot be explained, but a name for the moment in which noise takes on a shape and looks back.
